categories.name: Direct Payment
categories.description: Cases where the fine is created and promptly paid with very short trace lengths and durations, often without involving extensive notification or penalty steps.
categories.rationale: High frequency among low-duration and low-length variants (e.g., V0002, V0007), representing straightforward fine settlements.

categories.name: Standard Collection / Credit Referral
categories.description: Cases that progress through standard notifications and penalties over a moderate to long duration, ultimately culminating in credit collection.
categories.rationale: Dominates the high-frequency long-duration tail of the log where fines remain unpaid and are escalated (e.g., V0001, V0009).

categories.name: Delayed Payment with Penalties
categories.description: Cases where payment occurs after significant delays, intermediate notifications, penalties, and frequently exhibits repeated payment transactions.
categories.rationale: Represents the cluster of variants featuring standard notifications, added penalties, and multiple recurring payment steps (e.g., V0004, V0005, V0006).

categories.name: Appeals and Legal Proceedings
categories.description: Complex cases involving formal appeals to the prefecture or judge, resulting in extended durations, prefecture results, and alternative resolution paths.
categories.rationale: Captures variants explicitly containing appeal-related activities such as Send Appeal to Prefecture and Appeal to Judge (e.g., V0008, V0057, V0103).

categories.name: Payment Rework Loops
categories.description: Outlier variants characterized by an exceptionally high trace length driven by repetitive, sequential payment installments or iterative transactional rework.
categories.rationale: Identified by extreme length and repetition of payment events over prolonged periods (e.g., V0153, V0151, V0147, V0224).
